# ADR: Bottom Navigation Structure

## Status
OPEN — decision needed before Workshop tab can be placed

## Context
App has 5 bottom-nav tabs: Builds, Colonies, Traders, Resources, Notes.
Need to add a 'Workshop' section (custom build import, management, future build-builder).
5 tabs already feels cramped on small phones. Adding a 6th is not desirable.

## Options

### A — Replace Resources with Workshop; Resources moves inside Workshop
- Pro: no extra tab, Workshop has full section
- Con: Resources loses top-level visibility; user who uses it daily loses one tap
- Con: Resources and Workshop are thematically unrelated (game reference vs build tooling)

### B — Add 6th Workshop tab, keep all 5
- Pro: everything visible, nothing displaced
- Con: 6 tabs on 375px phone = ~62px each, very cramped
- Con: icons lose labels or become unreadable

### C — 'More' overflow: 4 core tabs + More (lists Resources, Workshop, future)
- Pro: scales to any number of sections
- Pro: core nav stays uncluttered
- Con: Resources and Workshop both hidden behind extra tap
- Con: less discoverable

### D — Move Resources into Traders (game economy reference)
- Pro: frees a slot for Workshop at top level
- Con: Resources covers people/food/materials/etc — not just trader items; weak fit

### E — Workshop as header action (gear icon top-left)
- Pro: zero nav impact
- Con: not discoverable, breaks the section model, header already has update badge top-right

### F — Drawer / hamburger replacing one tab
- Pro: scales well, iOS-familiar pattern
- Con: adds complexity, inconsistent with current sheet-based interaction model

## Constraints
- Must work one-handed on iPhone SE (375px wide)
- Workshop must be reachable in ≤2 taps
- Resources must not be effectively hidden from regular users

## Decision
TBD

## Consequences
Blocks: T-W1 (Workshop tab placement)
Does NOT block: T-W3 (storage/merge), T-W6 (custom chars) — those are pure logic
